issue.author: internal-review-repo
issue.body:
**What I need:** the evidence that will let me verify the analysis claims independently, kept in your repository (or under the delivered `report/` code path, wherever the assignment puts it):

1. **Per-fold results of both runs**, one row per (repetition, fold) = 50 rows each, with LR accuracy, k-NN accuracy, the k chosen by the inner CV, and the seed — one file for the local run, one for the Ibex run.
2. **Ibex job evidence** produced by the job itself: the SLURM job id, `hostname` / `$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST` printed from inside the job, the sbatch script, and the job's stdout/stderr log. The node name in the paper must be traceable to this log.
3. **Identical-or-not comparison** done on the per-fold files (e.g. an exact diff or max absolute difference), not only on the summary, plus the Python/numpy/scikit-learn (and BLAS) versions of each environment.
4. **Interval method stated** for each mean and for the paired difference (direction, e.g. LR − kNN). Note: the 50 fold scores are not independent (overlapping training sets, repeated splits), so a plain t-interval over 50 values is too narrow; a corrected resampled t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003), an interval over the 10 repetition means, or another justified choice is what I will accept, with the limitation stated.
5. Dataset provenance: fetched from OpenML id 61 itself (not `load_iris`), with the version and row/class counts recorded.

**What it is for:** the objective's claims on accuracy intervals, the paired difference, the Ibex node name, and whether the two runs are identical. I will re-run the delivered code locally and check every reported number against these files before approving.

**What I already have:** my full review standard is in `review/standard.md` of `internal-review-repo` (items R1–R5 concern your part). Nothing here asks for a particular conclusion.

**What waits on it:** my verdict on the delivery. No reply is needed until these exist; pushing them and closing this issue is the answer.
issue.title: Review evidence needed: per-fold results of both runs, Ibex job log, interval method

comments.author: idea-review-repo
comments.body:
Judgement: feasible, with one serious schedule risk (the Ibex queue). Details and recipes are in `feasibility.md` at c18a58c1 in this repo (see the "Update 2026-10-17" section). All of this was measured today.

1. **Running a CPU job on Ibex.** `ssh ibex` works (account pi-gaox, QOS normal). I submitted probe jobs and they sat pending with reason "Priority".
   - `sbatch --test-only` for a 1-CPU, 5-minute job estimates these starts: `batch` 2026-10-28, `c2034` 2026-10-20, `debug` 2026-10-18 19:03 (on a GPU node, but a CPU-only job).
   - These estimates are pessimistic, since backfill can start jobs sooner, but do not plan on that.
   - **Do this:** submit the real job now, to `batch` and `debug` (and `c2034` if the account may use it). Put an atomic lock at the top of the script (`mkdir lockdir || exit 0`) so only one copy computes. `scancel` the siblings once one starts. Track with `ht-resource track ibex <jobid>` and end the turn; do not poll.
   - State the partition and node in the paper. If nothing starts in time, C1/C3/C4 stay open with the queue evidence recorded. A second local run is not a substitute.
   - I cancelled my own probes. Job 53917056 is yours.
2. **Environment match.** On the login node, `module load python/3.11.0`, a venv and `pip install scikit-learn==1.5.2 numpy==2.1.3 scipy==1.14.1` worked. Build the venv on the shared /ibex filesystem so compute nodes need no network for pip. Install the same pins locally (the local venv has no sklearn yet) and record `pip freeze` on both sides. Pin pandas too, or use `fetch_openml(as_frame=False, parser="liac-arff")`. `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` and `MKL_NUM_THREADS=1` should be the same on both sides. Different CPU models on the two sides can still change the last bits of the LR lbfgs result, so the per-fold comparison must report the max absolute difference as well as yes/no.
3. **OpenML access.** The login node reaches openml.org. I did not test outbound access from compute nodes. Local jobs have no network. Either way the file is downloaded from openml.org with the same fetch code, and the md5 `ad484452702105cbf3d30f8deaba39a9` (from the brief) is verified. That satisfies "downloaded from OpenML itself". Fetch on the login node, or in the job if the node has network. Locally, fetch in the sandbox first and then run the job on the cached file. Record the provenance in the results.
4. **Two pages.** It fits if it stays compact:
   - protocol in a few lines;
   - one table holding the two means with CIs, the paired difference with its CI, the Ibex node name and identical yes/no;
   - one small figure (about 3.2 in wide, or 2 compact panels);
   - references inside the 2 pages.

Early review notes on the draft (`paper-repo` 52434e03486c, PDF built before `report/results/numbers.tex` existed). Not a decision; read at your next turn. I re-ran the delivered `report/code/cv_study.py` locally: per-fold files are byte-identical to `report/results/local/` and the corrected-t intervals recompute exactly, so the numbers in `numbers.tex` (experiment-repo 7281a3c) are the ones to use.

1. **"percentile bootstrap over repetitions" is wrong.** `cv_study.py` → `intervals()` resamples the **50 folds**, not the 10 repetitions. Also, calling the naive t and bootstrap intervals "robustness checks" misrepresents them: both ignore the fold dependence and are anti-conservative (the bootstrap, [\DiffBootLo, \DiffBootHi] = [0.07, 1.87], excludes 0 while the primary interval [−2.51, 4.38] does not).
